openItems.explanation: Invoice HGC-26-0993 (Pier 9 Lofts, $96,400.00) was coded to Bellevue, the owner's billing office, but the job site is 2200 Elliott Shore Ave W, Seattle. Seattle taxes the work where it is done, so the draft reports it in Seattle and does not deduct it as taxed by Bellevue: $96,400.00 x 0.342% = $329.69 more city tax than the register's coding. A person corrects the coding; October's change order on the same job was coded the same way. No plug posted.

The state return is separate from this city return. The September 2026 state return reported HGC-26-0993 at location 1704 (10.30%); at the Seattle job-site rate of 10.55% the sales tax is $10,170.20 against $9,929.20 charged, $241.00 short. A person decides whether to amend that state return in My DOR and rebill the owner. This draft changes nothing on a state return. No plug posted.

Duwamish Gateway Logistics Center (J-2608) straddles the Seattle and Tukwila city line. All $1,994,700.00 of Q3 billings were coded to Seattle and the draft reports all of it: no deduction is claimed without evidence of where the work was done. The project manager's estimate of 60% in Seattle would take $797,880.00 out of Seattle, $2,728.75 less tax, but there is no survey or cost split, as the client's email confirms. A person obtains site evidence (the parcel survey and cost or labor hours by parcel) and decides; whether Tukwila imposes its own B&O tax decides which deduction line it would go on. No plug posted.

The draft deducts $48,200.00 for invoice HGC-25-0917 (Fremont Bakehouse LLC), written off September 30, 2026. Seattle allows the deduction only for revenue previously reported as taxable. The client's email says it was on the Q4 2025 Seattle return, but that return was not supplied. The $4,988.70 of sales tax written off is not a city deduction; it belongs on the state return. A person confirms before filing.

The Q3 return was due October 31, 2026 under the city's due date table, and the client's email says the date was missed. October 31, 2026 is a Saturday and the page checked does not say the date moves, so it has passed either way. Filed by November 30, the late fee is 9% of tax owed: $44,166.56 x 9% = $3,974.99, rising to 19% in the second month and 29% after. Interest also runs from the due date at the city's 2026 rate, which the page checked does not state. The city computes both when the return is filed; neither is in the draft total.

This is an unsigned draft in the return's classifications, not the city's form. The Seattle business license tax return is separate from the state combined excise returns: it is filed and paid in FileLocal, not My DOR, and the same receipts stay on the state returns too. A person reviews it, decides the open items and the retail treatment of Juniper Row Homes, 9 homes for a related speculative builder, and files and pays. Nothing has been filed or paid.
